reason: I’ll start building the rocky bodies by letting their constituent grains collide gently.
expectation: I expect the grains to stick into larger rocky aggregates, though not yet planetesimals.

alternatives.reason: I also considered starting with icy grains, but chose the rocky path first.

effect: Rocky pebbles have formed, but sticking alone will not carry them all the way to planetesimals.
reaction: The bouncing and fragmentation barrier makes the next stage more interesting.
reason: I’ll follow the rocky path and see how gas drag affects the pebbles.
expectation: I expect gas drag to change the pebbles’ orbits and help concentrate them, though the details are uncertain.

alternatives.reason: I could start the icy path instead, but prefer to continue with the rocky pebbles.

effect: Gas drag has put the rocky pebbles into drifting orbits, suggesting a way to concentrate them.
reaction: The distinction between inward drift and concentration is useful.
reason: I’ll use the pressure maximum to gather the drifting pebbles.
expectation: I expect the pebbles to accumulate near the pressure maximum, possibly forming a dense swarm.

alternatives.reason: I could begin the icy path, but I want to continue the rocky one first.

effect: The pressure maximum gathered the pebbles into a dense swarm, ready for gravity to take over.
reaction: It is satisfying to see a route around the sticking barrier.
reason: I’ll apply gravity to the dense rocky swarm to pursue the rocky planetesimal goal.
expectation: I expect the swarm to collapse into rocky planetesimals, though the result may be an intermediate stage.

alternatives.reason: I could start the icy path, but I want to finish the rocky path first.

effect: Gravity formed rocky planetesimals and completed the rocky goal; the icy goal remains.
reaction: The swarm collapsing into larger bodies neatly resolves the sticking problem.
reason: The only offered combination starts the icy planetesimal path.
expectation: I expect gentle collisions to form icy pebbles or aggregates.

effect: Icy pebbles have formed, providing material for the remaining planetesimal goal.
reaction: The mix of rock and volatile material is a useful distinction.
reason: The only offered combination should concentrate the icy pebbles, as with the rocky ones.
expectation: I expect a dense swarm of icy solids, though the result may differ from the rocky path.

effect: The icy pebbles have concentrated into a dense swarm, ready for gravitational collapse.
reaction: The parallel with the rocky path is clear, though somewhat repetitive.
reason: The only offered combination applies gravity to pursue the remaining icy planetesimal goal.
expectation: I expect the swarm to collapse into icy planetesimals, as the rocky swarm did.

effect: Gravity formed icy planetesimals and completed the remaining goal; they are possible water carriers, not the only source of terrestrial hydrogen.
reaction: The rock-and-ice mixture is useful context, though the collapse repeated the rocky path.

mostWorthwhile.text: Concentrating rocky pebbles and collapsing the swarm was most worthwhile: it showed how gravity can bypass the limits of sticking alone.

leastWorthwhile.text: The icy sequence felt repetitive after the rocky path, particularly its concentration and collapse.

surprise.text: The pressure maximum provided a way to gather solids rather than requiring every collision to make a larger pebble.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt purposeless, though the icy concentration compressed the gas-drag explanation into one step after the rocky path treated it separately.

continue.text: Yes, I would continue: the sticking barrier and gravitational workaround made me curious how these bodies develop further, despite the repeated icy sequence.
